run.procedureSummary: Step 1 (arrivals): add the cycle's new tickets to each team's open count, with no WIP cap applied. Step 2 (walk): go from team 1 to team 6 in order. If a team is over its WIP limit, cut it to the limit and pass the excess to the next team before checking that team, so overflow can cascade. Team 6's excess is closed-without-action and goes on the closed tally. Step 3 (status check): use the post-walk counts. A ROUTINE team at or above its Escalate mark goes ESCALATED. An ESCALATED team at or below its Stand-down mark goes ROUTINE. Otherwise status holds, and every flip is logged. Step 4 (work queues): every amount is computed from one post-walk snapshot and all moves are applied at once. A ROUTINE team closes floor(n/4), which goes on the tally. An ESCALATED team moves floor(n/2) to the team upstream (i-1). Team 1's bounce is closed and goes on the tally. Step 5 (backlog cut): total the board. If the total is strictly over 38, every team keeps floor(n/2) and the rest is closed and goes on the tally. At 38 or under, nothing happens. Closed tally starts at 0 and counts team-6 overflow, ROUTINE closures, team-1 bounces and backlog-cut closures.

openPoints.point: Order of operations inside step 4 (work the queues)
openPoints.assumption: All closures and bounces are computed from the same post-step-3 snapshot and applied together. Bounced-in tickets are not worked again in the same step.

openPoints.point: Whether the status check uses pre-walk or post-walk counts
openPoints.assumption: Post-walk counts, because steps finish board-wide in order: step 2 completes before step 3.
Excess passed to team i+1 counts toward team i+1's limit when the walk reaches it, so it can push further down the line (cycle 4: team 1 to team 2 to team 3, and so on).

openPoints.point: Where team 6's overflow and team 1's bounce go
openPoints.assumption: Both are closures and are added to the single closed tally.
Every quarter and half is rounded down per team. Backlog-cut closures per team are n - floor(n/2).
The cut fires only when the total is strictly greater than 38. Cycle 5 ends at exactly 38, so the cut does not fire.

openPoints.point: Teams over their limit after cycle 5
openPoints.assumption: Bounced tickets that leave a team over its limit after cycle 5 stay as they are, with no final walk. Team 2 ends at 10 (limit 8) and team 4 at 7 (limit 6).
Arrivals are added in full with no cap. Limits apply only in the step-2 walk.
